nodes.description: Public token symbol string, set once in constructor.
Public token name string, set once in constructor.
Public token decimals (8), set once in constructor.
Total token supply, written in constructor and read by totalSupply().
Mapping of account address to token balance; mutated by transfer and transferFrom.
Nested mapping of owner to spender to approved allowance; mutated by approve and approveAndCall.
Pure addition helper with overflow require check.
Pure subtraction helper with underflow require check.
Pure multiplication helper with overflow require check.
Pure division helper requiring a non-zero divisor.
Constructor that sets symbol, name, decimals, total supply and initial balance of the owner address.
Returns _totalSupply minus the balance of address(0).
Returns the token balance of tokenOwner.
Transfers tokens from msg.sender to the 'to' account using SafeMath.
Sets a spender allowance for msg.sender with no double-spend checks.
Transfers tokens from 'from' to 'to' while deducting the caller allowance.
Returns the remaining allowance of spender for tokenOwner.
Approves a spender and then invokes receiveApproval on that spender contract (external call).
Payable fallback that unconditionally reverts; contract rejects ETH.
External caller-controlled address used as balance/allowed owner index.
External call ApproveAndCallFallBack(spender).receiveApproval(...) executed after allowance state write without a guard.
Unchecked-style uint addition a + b guarded only by a require after the operation.
uint subtraction a - b guarded by require(b <= a).
uint multiplication a * b guarded by a post-hoc consistency require.
Recipient address parameter of transfer.
Token amount parameter of transfer.
Spender address parameter of approve.
Allowance amount parameter of approve.
Source address parameter of transferFrom.
Destination address parameter of transferFrom.
Token amount parameter of transferFrom.
Address whose balance is queried in balanceOf.
Allowance owner address parameter of allowance.
Allowance spender address parameter of allowance.
Spender contract address parameter of approveAndCall, target of the external call.
Allowance amount parameter of approveAndCall.
Arbitrary calldata forwarded to the spender's receiveApproval.

edges.reason: transfer reads and writes the balances mapping for msg.sender and the recipient.
transfer uses safeAdd to credit the recipient balance.
transfer uses safeSub to debit the sender balance.
approve writes the allowed mapping for msg.sender and spender.
transferFrom mutates balances[from] and balances[to].
transferFrom decrements allowed[from][msg.sender].
transferFrom uses safeAdd to credit the destination balance.
transferFrom uses safeSub for both balance and allowance deduction.
approveAndCall writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] before the external call.
approveAndCall performs an external call to the untrusted spender contract after the state write.
The spender contract can re-enter token functions during receiveApproval.
Control returns to approveAndCall after the untrusted receiveApproval callback.
allowance state written before the external call can be abused via re-entrancy.
msg.sender indexes the balances mapping, so the caller controls the debited account.
msg.sender is the owner key used when writing the allowed mapping.
transfer authorizes the operation purely on the caller-supplied msg.sender.
approve grants allowance on behalf of msg.sender without further checks.
transferFrom uses msg.sender as the spender key for allowance checks.
approveAndCall writes allowance and forwards msg.sender to the untrusted callee.
Constructor initializes _totalSupply.
Constructor assigns the entire supply to the fixed owner address.
Constructor sets the symbol state variable.
Constructor sets the name state variable.
Constructor sets the decimals state variable.
totalSupply reads _totalSupply.
totalSupply reads balances[address(0)] for the subtraction.
totalSupply performs an unguarded subtraction _totalSupply - balances[address(0)].
balanceOf reads the balances mapping.
allowance reads the allowed mapping.
safeAdd executes the addition operation on user-supplied uints.
safeSub executes the subtraction operation.
safeMul executes the multiplication operation.
The addition result is stored into balances, so overflow directly affects accounting.
The subtraction result is stored into balances, so underflow directly affects accounting.
transfer recipient parameter feeds the balances write.
transfer amount parameter feeds the SafeMath debit and credit.
approve spender parameter indexes the allowed mapping.
approve token amount parameter is stored as the allowance.
transferFrom source parameter indexes balances and allowed.
transferFrom destination parameter indexes the credited balance.
transferFrom amount parameter drives both SafeMath operations.
balanceOf owner parameter indexes the balances mapping.
allowance owner parameter indexes the allowed mapping.
allowance spender parameter indexes the allowed mapping.
approveAndCall spender parameter is both the allowance key and the external call target.
The attacker-controlled spender address determines which contract receives the callback.
approveAndCall amount parameter is stored as the allowance and forwarded.
approveAndCall data parameter is forwarded to the external callee.
Fallback rejects value transfers, blocking ETH-driven state changes.

normalization_plan.reason: The recipient address parameter has no independent semantic role outside transfer.
The amount parameter only exists to feed transfer's SafeMath arithmetic.
The spender parameter only indexes the allowed mapping inside approve.
The allowance value parameter is stored directly by approve.
The source parameter is only used to index balances and allowed inside transferFrom.
The destination parameter is only used to credit balances inside transferFrom.
The amount parameter drives the SafeMath operations of transferFrom.
The queried address is a trivial lookup key with no separate behaviour.
The owner key of the allowance lookup has no standalone semantics.
The spender key of the allowance lookup has no standalone semantics.
The spender parameter is the target of the unsafe external call and should be merged into that operation.
The amount parameter is only stored and forwarded by approveAndCall.
The data parameter exists solely to be forwarded into the untrusted external call.
